title: Tic-Tac-Toe: React, 0-2 Human Players
author: Operator (conversation); source retained by GitHub Copilot

questions: Before complete proposal composition, verify the selected main target's exact committed baseline and finish the repository Canon/tracker storage correction.

content.scope: Proposed product vocabulary and requirements for the tic-tac-toe feature in this PokerNight repository. Candidate identifiers are not admitted Canon identities.

d-human-count.text: The number of human-controlled marks in a game: zero, one or two. Zero players means zero human players; X and O still exist and are controlled by AI.

d-ai.text: A computer-controlled player. Unbeatable means no loss from a fresh legal game against any legal opponent sequence as either X or O. A draw is valid, not a guarantee of victory. Two unbeatable AIs draw under standard rules. This does not select an algorithm or external AI service.

d-game.text: One standard 3x3 round from an empty board until X wins, O wins or a draw. It is distinct from a browser session and implies no match or multi-game score.

d-replay.text: Play again is a person's explicit action beginning another game after termination. In zero-human mode the person triggers replay without controlling either mark. Replay is not automatic.

r-rules.text: Use nine cells in a 3x3 board. X starts; X and O alternate, placing one mark in an empty cell. Three identical marks in a row, column or diagonal win. A full board without a winner draws. A winning final move takes precedence over draw; terminal games accept no moves.
acceptance: All eight winning lines for both marks
Full-board draw and winning ninth move
Occupied-cell rejection, X-first alternation and terminal immutability

r-modes.text: Support zero humans with AI controlling both marks, one human versus AI, and two humans sharing one device. Human input cannot place moves on an AI-controlled turn.
acceptance: Complete a game in each mode
Zero-human games progress without board input after Start
Two-human games schedule no autonomous moves
The phone runs its own local game, not a synchronized second board

r-mark-choice.text: Before a one-human game, choose human X or O; AI controls the other mark.
acceptance: Human X makes the opening move after Start
Human O receives an opening AI-X move after Start and the AI delay

r-unbeatable.text: Every AI-controlled mark must be unbeatable as defined by d-ai. Algorithm and library selection remain implementation choices.
acceptance: Exhaust every legal opponent sequence from a fresh game for AI-X and AI-O, with zero AI losses
Every chosen move is legal
Cover every permitted nondeterministic tie-breaking choice
AI versus AI terminates in a draw; winning against perfect play is not promised

r-result.text: Show the current turn and unambiguous X win, O win or draw. Preserve the finished board and result while waiting for a new-game action.
acceptance: Labels agree with the board
Waiting after AI versus AI finishes neither clears the result nor schedules a new game

r-manual-replay.text: Provide Play again after termination in every mode. One activation clears the board/result and starts exactly one game with X first, retaining the displayed mode and mark selections without another Start confirmation.
acceptance: No automatic replay after any waiting period
Replay works in all three modes and for each terminal result
No duplicate new games or delayed moves from the prior game

r-react.text: Implement the actual interactive game interface in React. No bundler or language variant is prescribed.
acceptance: The delivered browser application uses React for its game interface

r-runtime.text: Use local Node.js and Express to serve the React application on fixed port 3630. Versions, commands and build/serving details follow the repository implementation context.
acceptance: Load assets and complete a game through port 3630
If port 3630 is occupied, report an actionable startup error instead of silently choosing another port
Use deliberate local Wi-Fi access for the physical phone; do not treat phone localhost as the host

r-browsers.text: Support Chrome on desktop and Chrome on a physical iPhone accessing the local server over Wi-Fi. Responsive layout, pointer/touch controls and complete game/replay behavior are required. Other browser families are optional supplemental testing, not additional release gates.
acceptance: Board, mode/mark controls, Start, turn/result and Play again remain accessible without overlap or clipping
Game rules do not change with viewport size
Test actual desktop Chrome and actual iPhone Chrome; emulation or another mobile browser cannot substitute
Record desktop OS, iPhone model/iOS version, Chrome versions, real viewport and local access URL

r-local-session.text: Keep play shared-device and local to a browser session, without accounts, saved games or persistent scores. No synchronized cross-device multiplayer or scoreboard is inferred.
acceptance: No account flow, saved-game feature or persistent-score behavior
Separate browser sessions do not share a board

r-ai-pacing.text: Schedule each AI move with a 500 ms delay before applying it, including opening moves and every AI/AI turn. Browser scheduling can run later under background throttling or load; this is not a hard real-time deadline.
acceptance: Controlled-clock tests show no move before the delay and one legal move when its turn runs
Foreground observation shows distinct moves
Moves occur only in the current active game's AI turn, never after termination or from stale games
Stacked callbacks cannot apply multiple moves

r-state-authority.text: The browser owns transient board, controller, AI, turn and terminal-result transitions; Express serves the app. No server gameplay API or shared cross-device state is required. This does not promise offline asset loading.
acceptance: Gameplay does not depend on server move-validation or opponent endpoints
Independent browser sessions keep independent boards
No saved-game or persistent-score behavior, while replay retains current settings

r-start-setup.text: Allow mode selection and one-human X/O choice before Start. No human or AI move happens before Start. Start begins with X; lock mode/mark changes during active play and enable them again after termination. Editing terminal settings alone does not start a game. Preserve the finished board/result until an explicit new-game action.
acceptance: Exercise Start in all modes
Human O and AI/AI opening moves occur only after Start and the 500 ms delay
Active setup controls cannot change controller ownership
Terminal setup becomes usable but schedules no move on its own
Play again starts directly using displayed selections, without a second Start

s-solo.text: Choose X/O, press Start, play an unbeatable AI and replay with the same selections.

s-watch.text: Press Start to observe two unbeatable AIs with 500 ms pacing, retain the draw and choose when to Play again.

s-two-humans.text: Two people share a device, start, alternate legal moves, see the result and choose replay.

s-local-browser.text: Use desktop Chrome or physical-iPhone Chrome over local Wi-Fi to play the browser-held React game served by Express on port 3630.

implementation_choices: Product source placement and compatible toolchain versions
Maintained game/AI library and independently verified behavior
Component structure, internal APIs and React state implementation
Local bind/access setup without unauthorized firewall changes
authority_limits: No complete proposal or implementation permission
No inherited independent review or approval

questions: Inspect this repository's product/toolchain conventions before assigning implementation paths.
Finalize the complete phase contract against a freshly verified committed main baseline after the Canon/tracker storage correction.

w-playable-game.title: Playable local React tic-tac-toe with verified unbeatable AI
w-playable-game.outcome: One cohesive delivery of the browser-held game, local Express serving on 3630, exhaustive correctness/AI tests and actual Chrome desktop/iPhone acceptance. Internal tasks are not separately reserved phases.
included: Standard rules and all human-player modes
Explicit Start and active setup lock
Manual replay in every mode with current settings
React served by local Node.js/Express on 3630
excluded: Framework helper changes as product work

tasks.text: Inspect repository conventions, packages/tests and compatible dependencies. Evaluate a suitable maintained game/AI library for license, browser compatibility, footprint, rules and unbeatable behavior. If none is suitable, request an explicit tradeoff decision rather than silently writing a custom engine.
Integrate rules/AI and independently verify legal transitions and no losses for either AI mark. Internal API choices remain implementation decisions.
Implement React setup, Start, controller ownership, turn/result display, 500 ms AI turns, manual replay and cancellation or rejection of stale callbacks. Add behavior/component tests.
Serve built React assets through Express on 3630. Document run commands and deliberate LAN access; verify occupied-port refusal.
Verify the integrated application automatically and on actual desktop Chrome and physical-iPhone Chrome. Record exact implementation and environment evidence.

acceptance: Rules cover all eight win lines for X/O, full draw, final-cell win precedence, X-first alternation, occupied cells and terminal immutability.

Explore every legal opponent sequence against AI-X and AI-O, all permitted nondeterministic choices, legal returned moves and zero AI losses. Use an independent outcome oracle or assertions separate from the engine being tested. AI/AI must draw.
All modes remain inactive before Start. One-human mode accepts input only for the human turn; two-human mode schedules no AI moves; zero-human play needs no board input after Start.

Controlled clocks verify no move before 500 ms and exactly one legal move for the scheduled turn, including openings and successive AI/AI turns. Cover rapid input, stacked timers, termination and stale prior-game callbacks.
Lock mode/mark during play; unlock at completion. Changing terminal setup alone does not start moves. Play again starts directly with displayed selections, X first and no duplicate game.
Each reachable terminal result persists until a new-game action. Replay clears board/result, retains mode/mark and isolates old callbacks.
Verify browser-owned state and independent sessions without move APIs, authentication claims, saved games or persistent scores. No offline-loading guarantee is inferred.
Load real React assets and play through port 3630; occupied port fails clearly. Verify actual phone/LAN URL without assuming phone localhost or changing firewall/public exposure without authority.

Complete/replay games in actual desktop Chrome and actual Chrome on the physical iPhone. Exercise touch/pointer input, setup, Start, AI observation, result retention, full board/control fit, hit targets and stable non-overlapping layout.

Record device, OS, browser versions, viewport, URL, tested commit, observed outcomes, dependency versions, commands, automated results, AI exploration method/counts and untested cases. Screenshots support but do not replace interaction evidence.

recommended_supplemental_checks.status: engineering recommendations, adjustable with rationale; not claimed device dimensions
recommended_supplemental_checks.browsers: Firefox, Safari, Android, Chromium emulation and WebKit checks are optional and cannot replace required actual Chrome desktop/iPhone evidence

risks: A purported unbeatable library needs exhaustive independent verification
Stale or duplicate scheduled moves can corrupt replay and terminal state
Desktop emulation cannot prove iPhone Chrome behavior
LAN serving must remain deliberate local use without unauthorized network changes
later_contract_obligations: Resolve actual implementation placement/toolchain before naming paths
Provide the required validated architecture/pre-flight diagram when creating a complete phase prompt for these boundaries
Fresh exact baseline and independent review/decision are still required before admission
